stem.text: Let \( f(x) = -\sqrt[5]{x - 2} - 5 \). Determine whether f is differentiable at \( x = 2 \), and justify your answer.

answer_key.label: f is not differentiable at \( x = 2 \), because the difference quotient grows without bound, staying negative, on both sides, so the graph has a vertical tangent there.

worked_solution.text: f is continuous at \( x = 2 \), since \( f(2) = -5 \) and the root is continuous everywhere.
The difference quotient is \( \frac{f(2 + h) - f(2)}{h} = -h^{- \frac{4}{5}} \), and the exponent \( - \frac{4}{5} \) is negative.
Because the power of h has an even numerator, the quotient keeps the sign of -1 on both sides, and its size grows without bound as h approaches 0.
worked_solution.rule_named: one sided limits of the difference quotient

worked_solution.text: The difference quotient has no finite limit, so f is not differentiable at \( x = 2 \), and the graph has a vertical tangent there.

options.label: f is differentiable at \( x = 2 \), because f is continuous at \( x = 2 \), and every continuous function is differentiable.
options.derivation: differentiability concluded from continuity, the implication run backwards
